CUPED is a common way to reduce variance in A/B tests, and itâs very likely to come up in a data science interview. The usual version adjusts each market by its own pre-period metric, which can miss who actually shows up during the test.

I simulated a 60-market Airbnb experiment based on a recent Instacart post. Predicting each booking and averaging up to the market removed about half the variance, compared to 28% for standard CUPED.

Knowing that the covariate only needs to be unaffected by the treatment is the kind of follow-up that helps senior and staff data scientists stand out. Full tutorial and Colab notebook at the link in bio.

What does 666 actually mean?

Most people treat Revelation like a horror movie. They panic over the number and every scary headline.

The bookâs very first verse tells you who itâs about. Itâs the revelation of Jesus Christ (Revelation 1:1).

Revelation 13:18 says, âHere is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six.â

Six represents man, and 666 warns us about what happens when man tries to take Godâs place.

Satan builds what I call an unholy trinity, a fake version of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit with man sitting where God belongs. Each six is one of those seats.

The first is the Fatherâs seat as judge. We sit in it every time we decide what we deserve and what everybody else deserves.

With the second six, we push aside the Holy Spirit, who comforts and leads us, and numb the pain with whatever we reach for instead of bringing it to God.

The last six puts us in the Sonâs seat as Savior. Thatâs legalism, trying to make ourselves right with God by what we do. Ephesians 2:8-9 says, âFor by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.â

Understanding 666 shouldnât leave you fascinated with Satan. It should expose the places where youâve put yourself on Godâs throne and send you back to Jesus.

Those seats still belong to Him.

The bookâs very first verse tells you who itâs about. Itâs the revelation of Jesus Christ (Revelation 1:1).

Six represents man, and 666 warns us about what happens when man tries to take Godâs place.

Satan builds what I call an unholy trinity, a fake version of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit with man sitting where God belongs. Each six is one of those seats.

The first is the Fatherâs seat as judge. We sit in it every time we decide what we deserve and what everybody else deserves.

With the second six, we push aside the Holy Spirit, who comforts and leads us, and numb the pain with whatever we reach for instead of bringing it to God.

The last six puts us in the Sonâs seat as Savior. Thatâs legalism, trying to make ourselves right with God by what we do. Ephesians 2:8-9 says, âFor by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.â

Understanding 666 shouldnât leave you fascinated with Satan. It should expose the places where youâve put yourself on Godâs throne and send you back to Jesus.

Those seats still belong to Him.
